messages:
elaine: quick heads-up — after the rbac schema swap rolled at 02:15UTC we're seeing a small uptick in 'permission_change' audit entries referencing serviceacct tokens. KMS access logs show a handful of decrypts from a pod that shouldn't have requester_role perms. tagging sec + infra :eyes:

samir: can you paste the audit query you used? want to double-check scope before we panic.

elaine: yup. ran this against the audit_events table:```sql
SELECT actor, target_role, action, metadata->>'service' AS svc, created_at
FROM audit_events
WHERE action = 'role_assign' AND created_at > now() - interval '60 minutes'
ORDER BY created_at DESC
LIMIT 50;
```

henry: thanks. looks like three assigns came from the churner job (k8s pod) that should only write tags, not role_assign. possible migration pod picked up wrong env? :thinking_face:

natasha: running the KMS access query now to correlate:```bash
gcloud logging read "protoPayload.methodName=\"google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt\" AND resource.labels.project_id=\"redwood-prod\"" --limit 50 --format json
```

security-bot: ALERT: 6 decrypt operations from service "churner" in last 15m. No IAM policy change recorded in acl-audit. Flagging for manual review.

ops-oncall: do we need to pause the rollout? canary shows elevated error rate but not total outage.

samir: short answer — pause the schema rollout and scale down the migration job to 0 replicas while we triage. I'll open a stop-deploy in the release channel.

elaine: agreed. natasha — can you snapshot the affected audit rows and KMS logs and drop into #sec-incident-summaries? include the full serviceacct IDs.

natasha: done. pasted a sanitized set (removed sensitive tokens) to #sec-incident-summaries with correlation ids. sample log:```json
{
  "timestamp":"2026-03-20T02:23:14Z",
  "principal":"svc-churner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
  "action":"Decrypt",
  "key":"projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/main/cryptoKeys/secret-kms",
  "request_id":"req-9a7b"
}
```

henry: next steps from infra side: revert the migration pod image to last known-good (v2.1.4), redeploy with rbac debug flags off, and run a limited canary on shard-a only.

samir: security note — we should treat this as a privilege escalation near-miss until proven otherwise. start vuln triage flow, get a quick timeline and list of impacted customers (if any) by EOD. I'll coordinate with support.

elaine: adding audit checklist: 1) confirm which assignments were automated vs manual, 2) KMS decrypt reasons, 3) cross-check service account policies for unexpected bindings, 4) rotate any exposed keys if confirmed.

ops-oncall: I'm standing by to perform key rotation if asked. let me know the exact key ids and window to rotate.

natasha: ETA 45m for the initial correlation doc. putting a manifest of suspect serviceaccts in the thread.

samir: good. also pushing a short-term monitoring rule: alert if any role_assign originates from pods in the infra namespace (should only come from controlplane). will bake into alerting later.

elaine: filing a post-deploy postmortem template now — we'll include timeline, root cause hypothesis (migration job reading wrong env var / role mapper table mismatch), mitigations (pause, revert, rotate keys if needed), and long-term fixes (stronger changeguard, unit tests for migration).

henry: one last note — if we discover any customer-visible exposure, we need legal and compliance loop in ASAP. samir will ping them.

samir: pinged legal/compliance and support. marking this high priority. :white_check_mark:

elaine: thanks everyone. keep replies inline here for triage notes only. will update thread when we have confirmation.
